Welcome to my personal website! I'm Varun Vaidhiya, a Software Engineer based in the UK working on AI, Robotics, and Performance Optimisation.

I'll be sharing thoughts on:
AI model benchmarking and performance optimisation on edge hardware
Robotics — ROS, sensor fusion, autonomous systems
Low-level programming — ARM architecture, embedded systems
Open source projects I'm building and shipping

Everything I build lands on GitHub — feel free to fork, remix, or contribute.

Stay tuned for more posts. If you'd like to connect, find me on X/Twitter or LinkedIn.
chunks.title: Hello World
chunks.heading: Hello World

chunks.text:
Here's a collection of projects I've been building. All code is open source on GitHub.

Production-ready toolkit to run AI locally

A Kotlin SDK designed to make running AI models locally straightforward and production-grade. Built with a focus on ease of use and reliability for on-device AI inference.

View on GitHub →

AI inference on ARM hardware

Exploring and optimising AI model inference on ARM-based hardware. This project is about understanding how to get the best performance from AI models running on ARM chips — from setup through benchmarking.

View on GitHub →

ROS-based mecanum wheel robot
chunks.title: My Open Source Projects
chunks.heading: My Open Source Projects

chunks.text:
A robotics project using ROS (Robot Operating System) to control a mecanum wheel robot. Covers locomotion, motion planning, and sensor integration.

View on GitHub →

SAM2 model applied to autonomous vehicles

Applying Meta's Segment Anything Model 2 (SAM2) to autonomous vehicle perception tasks. Explores zero-shot segmentation for AV sensor data.

View on GitHub →

Automatic Emergency Braking — Model-Based Design

A model-based design implementation of an Automatic Emergency Braking (AEB) system, a safety-critical feature in modern vehicles.

View on GitHub →

Performance analysis with Perfetto
chunks.title: My Open Source Projects
chunks.heading: Mecanum-Wheel-Robot

chunks.text:
Python scripts for capturing and analysing system traces using Google's Perfetto tracing tool. Useful for deep-diving into CPU scheduling, memory, and I/O behaviour.

View on GitHub →

Open-source drivers for Kinect for Windows v2

Forked and contributed to the open-source driver for Microsoft Kinect v2, enabling depth camera access on Linux and macOS.

View on GitHub →

Decentralised voting with fingerprint authentication

A blockchain-based voting system that uses MFS100 fingerprint scanner authentication to ensure secure, verifiable, and tamper-proof elections.

View on GitHub →

chunks.text:
Hi, I'm Varun Vaidhiya — a Software Engineer based in the UK , working at the intersection of AI, Robotics, and systems-level performance. 
 My focus is on optimising AI models through benchmarking , understanding low-level hardware behaviour , and delivering best-in-class solutions for performance-critical systems. I'm particularly interested in running AI efficiently on edge hardware and ARM architectures. 
 I build what excites me and release it all as open source — from ROS-based robots and AI inference toolkits to blockchain applications and data science case studies.
chunks.title: About

chunks.text:
AI & Performance Optimisation — Benchmarking AI models, profiling with Perfetto, and squeezing performance out of constrained hardware
Robotics — ROS-based systems, autonomous vehicles, sensor fusion (Kinect v2, LiDAR)
Low-level Programming — ARM architecture, embedded systems, hardware-software co-design
AI on Edge / Arm — Making AI inference efficient on ARM and mobile devices
ML & Data Science — EDA, predictive modelling, classification, SQL analytics
